summary: Kenneth G. Zysk is an indologist and historian/archaeologist. He earned an M.A. at UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. at Australian National University. He held posts at Eastern Michigan University, UC Los Angeles, Wisconsin-Madison, Toronto, and the University of Copenhagen.

Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. He studied at Columbia University, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and the CUNY Graduate Center, also studying under Aloysius Pieris. He held academic posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara circa 1908–1912. He served as Professor of the History of Religion at Pacific School of Religion and Lecturer at the University of California (~1921–1935).

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who taught Jay L. Garfield. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and chaired both the Numata Center (1996–1999) and Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (until 1999).

Buddhist studies scholar Kenneth K. Tanaka studied at Stanford, CSU, Institute of Buddhist Studies, Eastern Institute, University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held faculty posts at IBS, UC Berkeley, and Musashino University, serving as professor and director.

Kenneth R. Valpey works in religious studies, indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, taught Ravi M. Gupta, and held an academic post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Aichi Gakuin University (2000–2010), the University of Tokyo (professor from 2010), and Rissho University (professor, 2025).

Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He earned a doctorate in literature at Otani University and served as Professor Emeritus at Hanazono University (attested 2014, 2026).
Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He pursued his education at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) was a Buddhist studies and tibetology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University. He served as professor at Koyasan University (1926), Seizan College, and Shuchiin University (1955), and became Professor Emeritus at Ryukoku University in 1956.
Kenshi Kusano is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University and served as a professor there (attested 2006).

Kensuke Okamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2006) and is attested as a Ryukoku University professor at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute in 2026.

Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. He served as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 2015–2016).

Kenyu Mitomo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley, studying under teachers including Akira Hirakawa. He was Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (1968–2015).

Kevin A. Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Bates College and the University of Virginia, completing his doctoral studies under supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teacher Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa.

Kevin Buckelew works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College and was doctoral supervised by Bernard Faure, Chün-fang Yü, and Zhaohua Yang, alongside studying under Chao-heng Liao, Courtney Bender, Fumiko Nazikian, and Yan Ling.
Kexin Zheng is a researcher in Indology and religious studies. As of 2026, Zheng is a PhD candidate at Leiden University, studying under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop.

Khakyab Dorje (1871–1922) was an active figure in tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and others, and taught prominent students including Kalu Rinpoche and Karsé Kongtrul.
Kham Sum Zilnön Gyepa Dorjé was a scholar who studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Shenphen Nangwa. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (~2000–2004). He served as a professor at ITBMU (~2003) and as Fellow and Trustee at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (~2004).
